title: How Much Does Interior Painting Cost in Katy, TX?
description: Interior painting in Katy, TX typically runs $500–$1,500 per room or $3,000–$20,000+ for a full home. See what drives the price and get an accurate quote.
author: Chris Petkau
imageAlt: Interior painting in Katy, TX by The Proud Paintbrush.
content:
If you're planning a repaint in Katy, you're probably asking:

How much does interior painting cost in Katy, TX?

Most Katy homeowners pay between $500 and $1,500 per room, or roughly $2 to $4 per square foot of wall space once trim, baseboards, and prep work are factored in. A full interior repaint typically lands between $3,000 and $20,000+, depending on the size of the home, ceiling height, and how much prep and repair the surfaces need.

At The Proud Paintbrush, we paint interiors across Katy, Cinco Ranch, Cane Island, Falcon Point, and the rest of Fort Bend and West Harris County, so we see these numbers play out on real Katy homes every week. Here's what actually drives the price, and how to make sure the number you're quoted is realistic.

How Much Does Interior Painting Cost in Katy, by Room?

These are general starting ranges, not fixed quotes. Every home is different.

Single room

$500 to $1,500

A bedroom, home office, or powder room with standard 9-foot ceilings and light prep usually falls in this range.

Multiple rooms

$1,500 to $5,000

Common when homeowners repaint a living area, hallway, and a bedroom or two in the same visit.

Full interior

$3,000 to $20,000+

This covers a whole-home repaint — walls, ceilings, trim, and doors throughout the house. Larger Katy floor plans in neighborhoods like Cinco Ranch and Cane Island tend to land toward the higher end simply because there is more square footage and more rooms to cover.

For the full rate sheet behind these numbers, see our detailed interior painting price list. If you're budgeting for exterior work at the same time, check our full house painting cost guide for Katy for combined interior and exterior ranges.

What Affects Interior Painting Cost in Katy?

Square footage matters, but it's rarely the only thing that moves the price.

1. Square footage and ceiling height

More wall area means more labor and material. Katy is full of newer two-story builds with vaulted entries, tray ceilings, and 10–12 foot great rooms — all of which take longer to prep, mask, and paint safely than a standard 9-foot ceiling.

2. Number of colors and coats

A single color throughout is the most efficient option. Multiple colors, accent walls, or a dark-to-light color change usually mean extra coats and more careful cutting-in, which adds time.

3. Trim, doors, and closets

Baseboards, door casings, closet interiors, and built-ins are priced separately from wall square footage because they require a different technique and more detail work. A room with a lot of trim will cost more than an identical room with none.

4. Prep and surface repair

Nail holes, drywall dings, caulking gaps, and glossy builder-grade trim all need attention before paint goes on. Prep is where a paint job either holds up for years or starts failing within months, and it's the single biggest factor separating a cheap bid from a lasting one.

5. Paint quality

We paint with Sherwin-Williams products because they hold color and stand up to daily wear better than budget paint. Better coverage also means fewer coats, which can offset some of the higher per-gallon cost.

What's Included in a Professional Interior Paint Job?

A proper interior painting scope covers more than just rolling color onto a wall:

  • Surface preparation — patching, sanding, and caulking

  • Protection of floors, furniture, and surrounding areas

  • Primer where needed for new drywall, stain blocking, or dark-to-light color changes

  • Professional paint application

  • Cleanup and a final walkthrough

  • Written warranty coverage

That's what separates a quote built around our interior prep process from a number pulled out of thin air.

How Does Katy Pricing Compare to Nearby Areas?

Interior painting rates in Katy are similar to what we quote in Sugar Land, Richmond, and Missouri City — the per-square-foot pricing doesn't really change by city. What does change is the typical scope.

Katy's housing stock skews newer, with a lot of production and semi-custom homes in HOA communities like Cinco Ranch, Grand Lakes, Falcon Point, and Cane Island. These homes often have larger great rooms, taller ceilings, and more open floor plans than older Sugar Land or Richmond homes, which can push a full-interior quote toward the higher end of the range even when the paint and process are identical. HOA guidelines in some Katy neighborhoods can also affect exterior color choices, though they rarely restrict interior colors.

If you want the specifics for your neighborhood, our interior painting services in Katy page has more on what we typically see across Katy homes.

Is It Worth Paying More for a Professional Painter?

In most cases, yes — and it's usually not close.

A cheap bid or a DIY weekend can look like the budget-friendly option upfront, but the real cost shows up later:

  • Skipped prep means nail holes, caulk lines, and patched drywall show through the finish within a few months.

  • Rushed cutting-in leaves crooked lines along ceilings, trim, and corners that are obvious in daylight.

  • Cheap paint fades, flattens, or scuffs faster, especially in high-traffic hallways and kitchens.

  • A redo costs more than doing it right the first time — you're paying for labor and material twice.

A professional crew brings proper prep, clean lines, and a paint system suited to how the room is actually used, backed by a written warranty instead of a handshake.

What Add-Ons Can Increase the Cost?

These are commonly bundled into an interior painting project and will move the total up from the base room or square-footage price:

  • Ceiling painting

  • Trim and baseboard detailing

  • Drywall repair

  • Wallpaper removal

  • Cabinet or vanity refinishing — see our cabinet painting price list

What Are the Red Flags of an Underpriced Bid?

A number that looks great on paper isn't a deal if the work doesn't hold up. Watch for:

  • A quote given over the phone or from a photo, with no one walking the actual rooms

  • No mention of prep, patching, or caulking in the scope of work

  • Vague language like "walls and trim" with no room-by-room breakdown

  • No proof of insurance or written warranty offered

  • Pressure to sign the same day or a price that expires within 24 hours

If prep work isn't itemized, it's usually because it isn't planned — and that's exactly where cheap paint jobs start to fail.

How Do I Get an Accurate Interior Painting Quote in Katy?

The only way to get a number you can actually trust is to have someone walk the rooms in person. A proper in-home estimate accounts for:

  • actual wall and ceiling square footage, not a guess based on home size

  • ceiling height and any vaulted or tray ceiling areas

  • the real condition of the walls, trim, and doors

  • how many colors and coats the job needs

  • what's included — trim, closets, doors, ceilings, or walls only

A phone estimate can only ever be a rough guess. If a company is willing to give you a firm number without seeing the space, that's a sign the number isn't firm at all. See our guide to defining your painting budget before your walkthrough so you know what questions to ask.

Frequently Asked Questions

How long does interior painting take?

A single room typically takes one day. A full interior repaint usually takes 3 to 7 days depending on the size of the home, the amount of prep needed, and the number of colors.

Do I need to move my furniture?

Not usually. We move and cover furniture as part of the job, though clearing small or fragile items ahead of time helps things move faster.

What's included in a quote?

A proper quote spells out exactly what's being painted (walls, ceilings, trim, doors, closets), the prep and repair work involved, the number of coats, and the paint product being used — not just a single lump-sum number.

Do I need to be home during the project?

You don't need to be present for the entire job, but we do recommend a walkthrough at the start and end so you can confirm colors, scope, and the finished result together.

How long does interior paint last?

With proper prep and quality materials, interior paint can last 5 to 10 years depending on the room and how much wear it sees.
